title: Pairwise OSCORE identity never matches IPv6 group roster
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

spec/12-apps.md 18.8.2 uses IPv6 node addresses for owner, admins, members, and join_key body[\"node\"] (example \"0200:...:3333\").

_bound_oscore_identity (35-50) accepts str as-is, or hex-encodes bytes, or recurses into durable_context_id(). _request_oscore_values (62-70) yields oscore_context before oscore_context_id. _pairwise_oscore_identity returns the first non-empty bound identity.

lichen.crypto.oscore.MemorySecurityContext.durable_context_id() returns bytes (sender-context id). If that object is bound as request.oscore_context (the post-unprotect path this file claims to require), the pairwise identity is hex(durable_context_id), not the peer IPv6 address.

Then:
- join_key: spec body[\"node\"] IPv6 != hex peer -> 4.03 even for the invited node
- requester_role(owner/admin/member IPv6) is None -> owner PUT/DELETE 4.03, roster pairwise 4.03
- if both a context object and oscore_context_id=\"0200::1111\" are set, the object wins and the IPv6 id is ignored

Tests mostly set oscore_context_id to the IPv6 string with no context object. test_join_key_accepts_bound_context_object invites the hex form, which is not the spec node address. This fails closed (no extra privilege) but makes owner/member authorization unusable on the real OSCORE binding.
acceptance_criteria: When request.oscore_context is a pairwise MemorySecurityContext and the peer node address is A, requester_role(id, A) and join_key body.node==A succeed for owner/member/admin A. hex(durable_context_id()) is not the roster key. Tests attach a real context object plus IPv6 owner/member, not only a string oscore_context_id.
